The average $\sigma_j(B)$s should then correspond to bounds for the $k$ quantiles of the eigenvalues of $A$ as in \eqref{eq:interlacing}.
In particular, after fixing $k$, our framework provides bounds in expectation on the $k$ spectrum quantiles of the kernel matrix $A$.
suppose we have $\mathrm{tr}\left(B^r/k\right)=\mathrm{tr}\left(A^r/n\right)$ for $1\leq r\leq k$
1-\epsilon\leq\frac{\mathbb{E}\left(\mathrm{tr}\left(B^r/k\right)\right)}{\mathbb{E}\left(\mathrm{tr}\left(A^r/n\right)\right)}\leq1+\epsilon

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and conclusion assert that the framework is proved to give (expected) bounds on the k spectrum quantiles of A. What is actually established is (i) an interlacing statement (cor:momentmatching) requiring exact equality of tr(B^r)/k and tr(A^r)/n for the specific matrices, and (ii) an approximate matching of expected traces up to a factor 1±ε (prop:momentmatch). The procedure then averages the j-th eigenvalue of B over m trials and applies the corollary to these averages. No result shows that averaged eigenvalues satisfy any moment condition (by Jensen, (1/k)Σ_j(Eσ_j)^r ≠ E[(1/k)Σ_jσ_j^r] for r≥2), nor that approximate expected moment matching yields quantile bounds (the paper itself notes via \cite{jinmusco} that this may fail). 'Corollary applies in expectation' has no formal content.

issues.failure_explanation: Equality of the first k moments of S and T does not imply equality of higher moments (e.g. S={0,1,2,3}, T={(3±√5)/2}: first two moments agree, fourth moments are 24.5 vs 23.5). The Chebyshev–Markov–Stieltjes bounds invoked need the polynomials P_0,…,P_k built from μ_0,…,μ_{2k} of S to be orthogonal for T, i.e. moments matching through order 2k−1 (Gauss quadrature); with k moments the b_i need not be roots of P_k. The statement itself is false: for k=3, T={1,2,3} (moments 2, 14/3, 12) and S with mass 0.34 at 0.9, 0.6588 at 2.556, 0.00117 at 8.549 (all nonnegative, same three moments) has more than n/3 of its points below b_min=1, violating the claimed bound (in the corollary's form, σ_{2n/3}(A) ≥ σ_3(B)); perturbing to distinct rational-weight configurations gives finite counterexamples with 3|n.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the hypothesis must be strengthened to moment matching for r=1,…,2k−1 (making the result the classical Chebyshev–Markov–Stieltjes inequality), and the framework's k-moment design and cor:momentmatching must be revised accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The 'very general interlacing theorem' and cor:momentmatching are false as stated. Since the whole framework is designed to match only k traces (prop:momentmatch, the sampling strategy), the theoretical basis for reading eigenvalues of B as quantile bounds of A collapses; a true version needs 2k−1 matched moments, which for an equal-weight k-point set is generally unattainable (Chebyshev-type quadrature).
issues.title: Interlacing proposition is false: matching only k moments does not imply the quantile sandwich (proof wrongly infers that all moments agree)
issues.why_classification: The headline theorem is false with explicit counterexamples; the only supported correction changes the hypothesis to one the rest of the paper cannot meet, so the framework's guarantee does not survive in comparable form.
